name: gaussian_majorana_recompilation
precondition: family dv_angle, needs rotations and needs two_qubit, measurement_free, 2 <= n <= 10. Declared check: every op of the (sub)circuit is a fermionic-linear-optics generator under Jordan-Wigner, i.e. v4.api.fermion.is_gaussian(ops) returns True on the whole op list, or on a maximal contiguous prefix/segment of it. On tfim_6 the fingerprint already reports free_fermion=true, majorana_planes=12, generator_algebra_rank=22, so the whole circuit qualifies; qft/qpe/hhl/qae are excluded at zero cost because is_gaussian fails (their rotations are not Majorana bilinears).
identity: A Jordan-Wigner Gaussian (matchgate / fermionic-linear-optics) circuit U acts on the 2n Majorana operators g_1..g_{2n} by conjugation as a single real orthogonal matrix R in O(2n): U g_a U^dag = sum_b R_{ab} g_b. R is a complete invariant of U up to global phase. So ANY circuit with the same R is the same unitary, regardless of its length. Procedure: (1) sweep the op list once accumulating R = orthogonal_of(ops) (12x12 here, each op contributes its own small orthogonal factor, so this is O(ops)); (2) factor R by Givens/Jacobi elimination, givens(R) -> a product of at most 2n(2n-1)/2 = 66 adjacent-plane rotations exp(theta_ab g_a g_b / 2) times a residual sign diagonal in O(2n) with det +-1; (3) emit(rotations, n) writes each plane rotation back as ONE Rz (same-site plane (2j-1,2j): bare rz on wire j) or one Rz conjugated by a short fixed Clifford ladder (cross-site plane: h/s plus a CX JW-string, all Clifford, zero T), and the sign diagonal as Z/S Cliffords; (4) drop every emitted plane whose |theta| is numerically zero, and keep only planes inside the support implied by generator_algebra_rank (22 here, so the realised count is well under 66). The output is a new op list with the SAME R and therefore the same unitary up to global phase, but with the rotation count set by the dimension of the Lie algebra rather than by the Trotter step count.
correctness: Under Jordan-Wigner the 2n Majoranas g_{2j-1} = Z_1..Z_{j-1} X_j, g_{2j} = Z_1..Z_{j-1} Y_j are Hermitian, anticommuting and generate the full operator algebra, so the map U -> R(U) = (adjoint action on span{g_a}) is a group homomorphism onto O(2n) whose kernel is global phase only (Jozsa-Miyake 2008, Terhal-DiVincenzo 2002). Hence R determines U up to a phase, and global phase is unobservable (project invariant 6). Each generator used here is Gaussian: an Rz(theta) on wire j is exp(-i theta Z_j/2) with Z_j = -i g_{2j-1} g_{2j} a bilinear; a nearest-neighbour ZZ/XX/YY Trotter term conjugated into the circuit is likewise a bilinear; H, S, CX/CZ in the matchgate patterns act as signed permutations/rotations on the g_a. Givens elimination of an orthogonal matrix is exact algebra (every factor is itself orthogonal, residual is a signed diagonal), so the only error is floating point in computing and factoring the 12x12 R; that is what the error_budget draw covers. The judge will check it in approximate mode (both sides carry off-grid Rz) with the phase-aligned operator distance on 6 qubits (64x64, cheap), plus the whole-circuit check against the ORIGINAL circuit, so a wrong R cannot be accepted. If is_gaussian or a distance check fails, the rule returns no match and nothing is charged.
trigger: Fires once per circuit (one match, the whole op list) when: (a) is_gaussian(ops) is True; (b) the number of off-grid rotations exceeds n(2n-1) = 66, i.e. there are more rotations than a Givens form can possibly need - on tfim_6 there are 160 > 66, so there is guaranteed redundancy; (c) majorana_rank(ops) <= 2n. If is_gaussian holds only on a maximal Gaussian segment rather than the full list, the match is that segment and the rewrite is spliced back in place (dependency-contiguous, so the splice is valid). Guard before returning the rewrite: price it (rotation count must strictly fall) and check sim.distance(old, new, 6)['op'] <= the drawn amount; otherwise emit no match.
expected_effect: tfim_6 is 160 off-grid Rz at eps_rz = 5e-4/160 = 3.1e-6 (8560 T total, ~53.5 T per rotation). The Givens form over O(12) needs at most 66 planes, and with generator_algebra_rank = 22 / majorana_planes = 12 the realised count should land near 60-66 non-zero planes; all the surrounding structure (sdg 102, h 192, cx 180, s 29, z 12) is replaced by the fixed Clifford JW ladders, which cost zero T. With N_Rz = 66 the per-rotation budget RISES to 5e-4/66 = 7.6e-6, so gridsynth's ~3*log2(1/eps_rz) cost per rotation falls slightly too, to ~52 T. Estimate 66 * 52 ~= 3430 T, i.e. 8560 -> ~3400. This is the one circuit where both baseline levers have exactly zero headroom (angle_cost 0, and pyzx/TKET/BQSKit-FT all sit at 8560) because none of them can see the fermionic structure: pyzx merges equal Pauli axes but the 22 distinct axis classes here are genuinely distinct as Paulis - they are only redundant as Majorana bilinears, which is a relation ZX calculus does not have. The floor tier's phase-gadget fusion therefore cannot reach this and is not being re-proposed: the compression here is in O(12), not in the Pauli group.
source: Jozsa & Miyake, 'Matchgates and classical simulation of quantum circuits', Proc. R. Soc. A 464 (2008); Terhal & DiVincenzo, PRA 65 032325 (2002); Kivlichan, McClean, Wiebe, Gidney, Aspuru-Guzik, Chan, Babbush, 'Quantum simulation of electronic structure with linear depth and connectivity', PRL 120 110501 (2018) (Givens-rotation networks for Gaussian circuits); Jiang, Sung, Kechedzhi, Smelyanskiy, Boixo, 'Quantum algorithms to simulate many-body physics of correlated fermions', PRApplied 9 044036 (2018)
